newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says 1997 budget not to exceed 56.5 bln DM.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says 1997 budget not to exceed 56.5 bln DM.

text.p: Germany's 1997 budget deficit will not exceed the planned level of 56.5 billion marks, despite lower tax revenues and higher unemployment outlays, Finance Minister Theo Waigel told parliament.
The deficit will be held below 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the level required for participation in European economic and monetary union (EMU), he reiterated.
Bonn will need to make a small supplementary payment, however, for the Federal Labour Office, he conceded, something he had earlier vowed to strike from the budget.

"The forecast by the six economic institutes that Germany's budget deficit will reach 3.5 percent of GDP is unfounded," Waigel said in a special session called by the opposition Social Democrats to discuss the budget.
"We will prove the opposite in the next 14 days," he said.
Parliament's budget committee will meet to discuss the 1997 budget on November 14.
